headline: Israeli forces withdraw from Hebron after 10-day siege
dek: Israeli forces have withdrawn from Hebron after a 10-day siege (imposed Oct 23 after a shooting attack that killed 2 IDF soldiers and wounded 3). Governor Dudin: Palestinian security forces have full control; displaced families can return.
sources: Khaled Dudin, Governor of Hebron, via Al Jazeera
fault_line: Was the 10-day siege security or collective punishment -- and who decides when it ends, the generals or the prime minister?

sections.what_happened: Israeli forces have withdrawn from Hebron after a 10-day siege (imposed Oct 23 after a shooting attack that killed 2 IDF soldiers and wounded 3). Governor Dudin: Palestinian security forces have full control; displaced families can return. Mayor al-Jaabari: municipality was officially informed at 6am (04:00 GMT); 'For the first time in 10 days, schoolchildren are going to their schools' -- 5 universities had been closed. Operation displaced: 537 families (AJ liveblog day-10 figure) vs Hebron Municipality 780 families / 4,969 people (via TRT) vs Al-Quds ~3,300 citizens -- figures DISAGREE and are recorded, not reconciled.
sections.what_verified: Al Jazeera (governor + mayor quotes) + TRT World (municipality figures) + Times of Israel (Palestinian media reports of withdrawal). Al-Quds carries no declared tier in the registry and is NOT counted.
sections.what_disputed: Scope contested: Times of Israel reports withdrawal from 'several neighborhoods' (11-day operation framing), vs governor's 'entire city'; IDF has NOT commented on the withdrawal. ToI also reports IDF Chief Zamir told Netanyahu there was no operational reason to continue the raid and no legal rationale to keep Palestinians from returning -- reportedly recommended ending it after day 2, but Netanyahu rejected that. Displaced-person counts disagree across sources (see claim).
sections.why_matters: End-of-siege beat with the split inside it: the army chief reportedly wanted it ended on day 2, it ran 10 days, and now the children are back in school -- but the IDF has not confirmed the withdrawal.
sections.context: Background: MISSED CATCH-UP (AJ published 06:27Z = 10:27 , missed by 1100 scan) -- Israeli forces withdraw from Hebron after 10-day siege; displaced families told they can return

totw_analysis: Our read: End-of-siege beat with the split inside it: the army chief reportedly wanted it ended on day 2, it ran 10 days, and now the children are back in school -- but the IDF has not confirmed the withdrawal. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Was the 10-day siege security or collective punishment -- and who decides when it ends, the generals or the prime minister?
